answer: Admission is paced by a wind-signed mesa watch. A newcomer escrows 1.73 POA for eleven epochs and plants a 20-byte stake on a public mesa board, bound to the escrow. Over 31 hours it must log four gale readings, at least 6 hours apart; each is a signed 13-byte quill mark mixed with the dusk beacon. Three unclustered clerks rebuild the marks from the live tip. If two stakes share a quill grain, or nine plantings arrive from one wallet in 58 minutes, each escrow is cut by 0.26 POA and both keys stay off that mesa for seven epochs. A missed gale reading extends the escrow and never auto-clears.
